content_html:
Blackout curtains often use a backing, foam, or laminated layer that can crack, stick, or delaminate under heat and aggressive washing. Before using a washing machine, follow the care label and treat the blackout coating as the most delicate part.

Identify whether the blackout layer is woven, foam, or coated

Inspect the back of the curtain and the care label. A woven blackout fabric often tolerates more handling than a bonded film or rubbery coating, which can be damaged by friction and heat.

Vacuum and spot-clean before washing the whole panel

Surface dust often comes off with low suction. For stains, test a barely damp cloth on a hidden corner and make sure the backing does not shed color, soften, or become tacky.

Avoid hot water and high-heat drying

Heat can distort synthetic layers and adhesives. If the label permits washing, use the specified cycle and temperature; do not improvise with a hot dryer to speed the process.

Air-dry according to the care instructions

Support the weight so the fabric does not stretch, and keep coated faces from sticking together while damp. If the blackout backing is already peeling, cleaning will not restore it and replacement may be more practical.
